title: Airline Crew Optimization & Rave Guide
excerpt: The definitive transition guide and technical compendium for developers entering the airline operations research and Jeppesen Rave space.
content_html:
✈️ Airline Crew Optimization & Jeppesen Rave: The Transition Guide

Version: 1.0.0
Domain: Airline Crew Pairing, Rostering, Resource Optimization, & DSL Engineering

Welcome to the definitive compendium for software engineers, optimization specialists, and operations researchers looking to transition into the Airline Crew Scheduling industry.

While general programming skills are highly transferable, the aviation sector operates on a highly specialized tech stack—most notably the Jeppesen CARMEN suite and its proprietary Rave domain-specific language (DSL). This repository bridges the gap, providing the domain knowledge, mathematical foundations, and technical references needed to confidently apply for roles like Rave Developer, Crew Optimization Engineer, or OR Analyst at major airlines (e.g., Norwegian, Lufthansa, Delta).

🎯 Target Audience

  • Software Engineers looking to transition into airline IT.
  • Operations Research (OR) Graduates needing practical industry context.
  • Current Airline Staff (Crew Planners, Schedulers) wanting to understand the technical side of the tools they use daily.

🗂️ Repository Structure

This compendium is designed to be read sequentially or used as a reference guide.

📖 Chapter Breakdown

📂 01. Domain Knowledge

You cannot write code for an airline if you do not understand how an airline operates. This section covers the business rules:

  • The difference between Crew Pairing (building anonymous flight sequences) and Crew Rostering (assigning sequences to named individuals).
  • Terminology like Deadheading (transporting crew as passengers), TAFB (Time Away From Base), and Block Time.

📂 02. The Jeppesen Ecosystem

Rave does not exist in a vacuum. It sits inside the CARMEN ecosystem. Here, we cover how developers use Python, Bash, and XML to marshal data in and out of the proprietary C/C++ solver engines, large-scale CI/CD regression testing, and integrating backend rules with the Studio GUI.

📂 03. Operations Research & Solver Mechanics

You don't need a PhD in math, but you must understand how your code impacts the solver. We break down Column Generation, heuristics, search space pruning, and how to debug the search tree when the solver rejects a specific flight connection.

📂 04. Rave Language Reference

Home to our Complete Guide & Technical Reference to the Jeppesen Rave Programming Language. This covers the declarative syntax, the hierarchical domain model (Leg \(\rightarrow\) Duty \(\rightarrow\) Trip), how to write efficient traversers (sum, any, all), enterprise codebase modularization, and how to profile your code for performance.

📂 05. Career & Interviews

A curated guide for breaking into the industry, featuring mock interview questions, technical assessments, and tips on how to pass the technical screening at airlines like Norwegian.

📂 06. Real-World Scenarios

Practical case studies demonstrating how to apply Rave to real-world airline problems, including Fatigue Risk Management Systems (FRMS), union seniority bidding, and dynamic day-of-ops disruption recovery.

🔗 External Resources & Further Reading

To truly master the intersection of software engineering, Rave DSL, and airline operations research, we highly recommend exploring the following external resources, whitepapers, and communities.

📚 Academic Papers & Core OR Concepts

  • "Airline Crew Scheduling: models, algorithms, and data sets" – A foundational paper by Kasirzadeh et al., covering the mathematical models behind crew pairing and rostering.
  • "Column Generation with a Rule Modelling Language for Airline Crew Pairing" – By Hjorring & Hansen, an excellent deep dive into how Rave rules directly integrate with column generation solvers.
  • "Using Semantic Analysis to Assist Schedule Optimization" – Master's thesis by Jacob Rippe (Chalmers University), detailing how ASTs and semantic inference are used to classify Final vs. Illegal Subchain rules inside the Rave compiler.
  • "DSL Engineering" – By Markus Voelter, an authoritative text on Domain-Specific Language design, separating concerns, and building modular language workbenches.

🏢 Industry Standards & Regulations

  • EASA Flight Time Limitations (FTL) FAQ – The official European Union Aviation Safety Agency guidelines on fatigue management. Essential reading for modeling hard constraints.
  • FAA Part 117 – The US equivalent of EASA FTL, detailing pilot flight and duty time limitations.

🌐 Operations Research Communities

  • AGIFORS (Airline Group of the International Federation of Operational Research Societies) – A professional society dedicated to the application of operations research in aviation. Their annual "Crew Management" study group presentations are a goldmine of modern industry practices.
  • INFORMS (Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences) – The premier international society for OR and analytics professionals.

💻 Tooling & Extensions

  • VS Code Rave Extension – The community-driven language server and syntax highlighter for writing Jeppesen Rave in Visual Studio Code.

👨‍💻 About the Author

Ole Christoffer Thorsen is a software engineer and optimization enthusiast specializing in the intersection of backend development, domain-specific languages (DSLs), and operations research.

Recognizing the steep learning curve for developers entering the aviation optimization space, the author built this compendium to demystify the Jeppesen CARMEN ecosystem, the Rave programming language, and the complex business rules governing airline crew scheduling.

  • Currently open to roles or projects as: Senior Rave Developer, Crew Optimization Engineer, or OR/Backend Software Engineer.

content_html_zh:
✈️ 航空公司机组人员优化和 Jeppesen Rave：过渡指南

版本：1.0.0 领域：航空公司机组人员配对、排班、资源优化和 DSL 工程

欢迎阅读针对希望进入航空公司机组调度行业的软件工程师、优化专家和运营研究人员的权威纲要。

虽然一般编程技能具有很强的可转移性，但航空业却在高度专业化的技术堆栈上运行——最著名的是 Jeppesen CARMEN 套件及其专有的 Rave 领域特定语言 (DSL)。 该存储库弥补了这一差距，提供了自信地申请主要航空公司（例如挪威航空、汉莎航空、达美航空）的 Rave 开发人员、机组优化工程师或 OR 分析师等职位所需的领域知识、数学基础和技术参考。

🎯 目标受众

  • 希望转型至航空公司 IT 领域的软件工程师。
  • 运筹学（OR）毕业生需要实际的行业背景。
  • 现任航空公司员工（机组计划员、调度员）希望了解他们日常使用的工具的技术方面。

🗂️ 存储库结构

本纲要旨在按顺序阅读或用作参考指南。

📂 01. 领域知识 ├── 📄 航空术语 101 ├── 📄 EASA FTL 法规 ├── 📄 联盟协议 (CBA) └── 📄 规划生命周期

📂 02. Jeppesen 生态系统 ├── 📄 CARMEN 系统架构 ├── 📄 Python 和 Bash 集成 ├── 📄 XML 数据结构 ├── 📄 测试和模拟 ├── 📄 CI/CD 和回归测试 └── 📄 Studio UI 和警告

📂 03. 运筹学 ├── 📄 组合优化 ├── 📄 列生成 ├── 📄 搜索空间和剪枝 ├── 📄 成本函数和惩罚 └── 📄 求解器跟踪和调试

📂 04. Rave 语言参考 ├── 📄 执行摘要和系统概述 ├── 📄 语言基础和语法 ├── 📄 层次结构和级别 ├── 📄 表达式、运算符和遍历器 ├── 📄 规则、合法性和搜索空间动态 ├── 📄 规则分类和语义分析 ├── 📄 成本建模和目标函数 ├── 📄 工作台和工具集成 ├── 📄 代码示例和案例研究 ├── 📄 最佳实践和常见陷阱 ├── 📄 高级语义分析（深入） ├── 📄 常见设计模式 ├── 📄 表格和数据查找├── 📄 性能分析 └── 📄 模块化和覆盖

📂 05. 职业与面试 ├── 📄 简历定制 ├── 📄 常见面试问题 └── 📄 模拟情景测试

📂 06. 现实场景 ├── 📄 疲劳风险管理 ├── 📄 联盟投标偏好 └── 📄 中断恢复

📖 章节分解

📂 01. 领域知识

如果您不了解航空公司的运营方式，则无法为航空公司编写代码。 本节涵盖业务规则：

  • 机组配对（构建匿名飞行序列）和机组排班（将序列分配给指定个人）之间的区别。
  • 像 Deadheading（将机组人员作为乘客运送）、TAFB（离开基地时间）和 Block Time 等术语。

📂 02. 杰普森生态系统

Rave 并不存在于真空中。 它位于 CARMEN 生态系统内。 在这里，我们将介绍开发人员如何使用 Python、Bash 和 XML 将数据编入和编出专有的 C/C++ 求解器引擎、大规模 CI/CD 回归测试以及将后端规则与 Studio GUI 集成。

📂 03. 运筹学与求解器机制

您不需要数学博士学位，但您必须了解您的代码如何影响求解器。 我们详细介绍了列生成、启发式、搜索空间修剪，以及当求解器拒绝特定航班连接时如何调试搜索树。

📂 04. Rave 语言参考

Jeppesen Rave 编程语言完整指南和技术参考的主页。 这涵盖了声明性语法、分层域模型（Leg \(\rightarrow\) Duty \(\rightarrow\) Trip）、如何编写高效的遍历器（sum、any、all）、企业代码库模块化以及如何分析代码的性能。

📂 05. 职业与面试

一本闯入该行业的精选指南，包括模拟面试问题、技术评估以及如何通过挪威航空公司等航空公司技术筛选的技巧。

📂 06. 真实场景

实际案例研究展示了如何将 Rave 应用于现实世界的航空公司问题，包括疲劳风险管理系统 (FRMS)、工会资历招标和动态运营日中断恢复。

🔗 外部资源和延伸阅读

为了真正掌握软件工程、Rave DSL 和航空公司运营研究的交叉点，我们强烈建议探索以下外部资源、白皮书和社区。

📚 学术论文和核心 OR 概念

  • “航空公司机组调度：模型、算法和数据集”——Kasirzadeh 等人的基础论文，涵盖机组配对和排班背后的数学模型。
  • “使用规则建模语言进行航空公司机组配对的列生成” – 由 Hjorring 和 Hansen 撰写，深入探讨了 Rave 规则如何直接与列生成求解器集成。
  • “使用语义分析协助调度优化”——Jacob Rippe（查尔姆斯大学）的硕士论文，详细介绍了如何使用 AST 和语义推理来对 Rave 编译器内的最终子链规则与非法子链规则进行分类。
  • “DSL 工程”——Markus Voelter 撰写，关于特定领域语言设计、分离关注点和构建模块化语言工作台的权威文本。

🏢 行业标准和法规

  • EASA 飞行时间限制 (FTL) 常见问题解答 – 欧盟航空安全局官方疲劳管理指南。 硬约束建模的必备读物。
  • FAA 第 117 部分 – 相当于美国的 EASA FTL，详细说明了飞行员飞行和执勤时间限制。

🌐 运筹学社区

  • AGIFORS（国际运筹学会联合会航空集团）——一个致力于运筹学在航空领域应用的专业协会。 他们的年度“船员管理”研究小组演讲是现代行业实践的金矿。
  • INFORMS（运筹学和管理科学研究所）——运筹学和分析专业人士的首要国际学会。

💻 工具和扩展

  • VS Code Rave 扩展 – 社区驱动的语言服务器和语法突出显示器，用于在 Visual Studio Code 中编写 Jeppesen Rave。
